title: What If Chain-of-Thought Is Not Enough?
abstract: arXiv:2611.26282v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reasoning capabilities in large language models have evolved from prompting-based methods to internalized model behaviors. In this paper, we investigate whether the internal thinking model of an LLM can be deliberately changed and whether such a change is beneficial. Instead of relying on Chain-of-Thought, we train models to follow Question--Option--Criteria (QOC), a structured decision process that decomposes a task into explicit questions, competing options, and evaluation criteria. We present a three-generation development pipeline that ranges from a basic QOC decision core to richer answer synthesis and statistically enriched QOC reasoning. We then evaluate the resulting models with respect to both internal consistency and output quality. translated_title: 如果思维链还不够用怎么办？
translated_abstract: 大语言模型的推理能力已经从基于提示的方法演变为内化的模型行为。本文研究大语言模型的内部思维模式能否被有意地改变，以及这种改变是否有益。我们不再依赖思维链，而是训练模型遵循“问题—选项—标准”这一结构化决策过程，将任务分解为明确的问题、相互竞争的备选选项以及评估标准。我们提出了一个三代发展流水线：从基础的QOC决策核心，到更丰富的答案合成，再到统计增强的QOC推理。随后，我们从内部一致性和输出质量两个方面对所得模型进行评估。在所报告的实验中，基于QOC的微调相较于未微调的基础模型提升了答案质量，并且当模型规模足够大、能够执行该过程时，收益尤为显著。（注：原摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出以“问题—选项—标准”（QOC）结构化决策过程替代思维链对大语言模型进行微调，并通过三代渐进式训练流水线证明该方法能显著提升答案质量，且模型规模越大收益越明显。
en_tdlr: This paper replaces Chain-of-Thought with a structured Question-Option-Criteria (QOC) decision process for fine-tuning LLMs, demonstrating through a three-generation training pipeline that QOC-based fine-tuning improves answer quality, with especially strong gains in larger models.
